land.text: Kakheti, Kukheti and Gardabani, which Grigol separated from the Principality of Iberia

predecessors.note: Principality of Kakheti page: Grigol separated from Iberia after Juansher's death in 787.

land.text: Kakheti and Hereti, annexed by David IV in 1104 and divided into the Duchy of Kakheti, the Duchy of Hereti, the Khornabuji bank and the Land of Arishini

successors.note: Infobox gives the last king as Aghsartan II (1102-1105); David IV's annexation is dated 1104 on the page.

capitals.name: Ujarma
capitals.note: Capital first at Ujarma, then moved to Tianeti in the mountains (undated on the page); Ujarma was handed to the Abkhazian king in 959.

capitals.name: Telavi
capitals.note: Kvirike III 'made Telavi his capital' and built a palace at Bodoji near Tianeti.

rulers.name: Grigol
rulers.title: chorepiscopus-prince
rulers.note: Chorepiscopi-princes' list from the Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti page; the Principality of Kakheti page gives reign years only for Grigol (787-827) and David (976-1010).

rulers.name: Kvirike III
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: The page's infobox treats 1014 as his first year as king; Bagrat III held Kakheti 1010-1014. The list shows Kvirike III twice and the dates inconsistently.

correction.text: Kakheti, Kukheti and Gardabani: the principality's first extent; Hereti 'bordered it to the southeast', the Aragvi river and the Emirate of Tbilisi to the west

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 787-1009. No area on either page. Kakheti's western reach in Shida Kartli (Grigol 'occupied Shida Kartli up to the Ksani river', then lost it to Abkhazia and Iberia) and the Abkhazian overlordship of the 930s-950s are not drawn; the Abkhazia dossier carries the vassal tint.

correction.text: Kakheti and Hereti united: 'from the Ksani River in the west to the Alijanchay River in the east, from Didoeti in the north, and south along the Mtkvari'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1014-1103, the kingdom of Kvirike III and his successors. Hereti is read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki, the same reading the Kingdom of Georgia dossier uses for its 1010 gain; the page gives rivers and no area. 1010-1013 is Georgian (Bagrat III).

ledger.note: 787: Grigol separates Kakheti from Iberia. 'Grigol separated from the Principality of Iberia after the death of Juansher in 787'; it 'initially covered Kakheti, Kukheti, and Gardabani', with Hereti to the southeast and the Aragvi and the Emirate of Tbilisi to the west.

1010: Bagrat III conquers Kakheti. 'Bagrat III invaded in 1010 and captured Kvirike III' (the Kakheti-Hereti page: Bagrat III annexed Kakheti 'in or around 1010'); David of Kakheti had been beaten by Bagrat in 1008. The Georgia dossier's 1010 gain names the whole Kakheti-Hereti; this page names Kakheti.

1014: Kvirike III recovers his crown after Bagrat III's death. 'Bagrat died in 1014, which let Kvirike III recover the crown'; the nobles restored him as King of Kakheti-Hereti and George I recognised the independence (Georgia dossier).

region.text: Hereti, read as Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax and Sheki

ledger.note: c. 1014: Kvirike III unites Kakheti and Hereti and crowns himself king. The kingdom 'emerged in c. 1014 AD' under Kvirike III 'who united Kakheti and Hereti'; the infobox places the Hereti incorporation in the 1010s and the Principality page gives 1010 as the union.

c. 1014: the chorepiscopal principality becomes the Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti. Kvirike III 'crowned himself king' and 'made Telavi his capital'; David (976-1010) was the last to hold the chorepiscopal title.

region.text: Kakheti and Hereti, annexed by David IV

ledger.note: 1104: Aghsartan II is handed to David IV and the kingdom falls. 'In 1104 Aghsartan II was arrested by the Areshiani princes of Hereti and handed to David IV', who 'finally annexed the kingdom to Unified Georgian realm'; it was divided into the Duchy of Kakheti, the Duchy of Hereti, the Khornabuji bank and the Land of Arishini; David IV appointed Arishiani governor (David IV page).

region.text: Kakheti and Hereti, joined to the Georgian realm

ledger.note: 1104: Kakheti-Hereti ends as a state and its lands become Georgian duchies (infobox: last king Aghsartan II, 1102-1105).

wars.name: Constantine III and Kvirike I against Hereti
wars.outcome: Kvirike I allied with Constantine III of Abkhazia, invaded Hereti and the allies divided its major strongholds.
wars.note: Strongholds only, so no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Abkhazian overlordship over Kakheti
wars.outcome: Padla II aided George II of Abkhazia in 925; under Kvirike II the Abkhazian king raided Kakheti and in 959 Kvirike's brother Shurta handed him Ujarma; 'Kakheti later reclaimed its lands after a truce with Leon III'.
wars.note: The George II page has George dispossess Kvirike II 'in the 930s' and die in 957 on an expedition against Kvirike's rebellion; the two pages differ on the order, so the span is the pages' outer dates.

wars.name: Sajid invasions of Kakheti
wars.outcome: 'Sajid invasions in 914 and 936 caused losses'; Hereti's king then reclaimed fortresses from Kakheti.
wars.note: No lands are named, so no zone.

wars.name: Bagrat III's conquest of Kakheti
wars.outcome: Bagrat III defeated David of Kakheti in 1008, invaded in 1010 and captured Kvirike III; Kakheti was recovered after Bagrat's death in 1014.

wars.name: Kakhetian-Georgian war against Fadhl II of Arran (Eklez River)
wars.outcome: Gagik's forces joined Bagrat IV's against Fadhl II of Arran, who was defeated at the Eklez River in 1027.
wars.note: 1022 reinforcements to George I against the Byzantines were beaten; c. 1029 an Alan invasion under Urdure was defeated; 1046-47 Gagik joined Liparit's rebellion against Bagrat IV. None moved a border.

wars.name: Seljuk submission and invasion of Kakheti-Hereti
wars.outcome: Aghsartan I submitted to Alp Arslan and agreed to pay tribute in 1068, fought Malik-Shah I's invasion in 1074 and embraced Islam and pledged loyalty to the Seljuks in the early 1080s.
wars.note: A tributary relation with the Seljuks, to be drawn as a vassal tint by the great-seljuk-empire dossier; the Seljuk wars page notes that Aghsartan 'went to the sultan to declare his submission'.

wars.name: David IV's annexation of Kakheti and Hereti
wars.outcome: Heretian nobles seized Aghsartan II and handed him to David IV, who annexed the kingdom; the lands became duchies under the Arishiani governor.
wars.note: David IV page: 'In 1104, a conspiracy led by the Heretian nobles Arishiani, Baram, and their uncle Kavtar Baramisdze deposed Aghsartan II' and David 'appointed the noble Arishiani as governor'.

certainty.note: The Kingdom page names rivers (Ksani, Alijanchay, Mtkvari) but no survey line; Kakheti's western Kartli border moved often.

notes: No Cliopatria row exists for Kakheti before 1468 (Kingdom of Kakheti, a different state, is eu-19-e). This dossier unites the Chorepiscopate/Principality of Kakheti (787-1010) and the Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti (1014-1104) as one state with a rename in 1014 (rule 2); the Georgia-dossier counterpart 'kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti' and the Abkhazia dossier's Kakheti vassal events use this slug. Differences to settle: (1) kingdom-of-georgia /ledger 1010 gains the whole Kakheti-Hereti (Zaqatala to Sheki included); the pages here say Bagrat III annexed Kakheti, and Hereti was a separate Kingdom of Hereti until Kvirike III united them c. 1014 (infobox: 'Hereti incorporation 1010s'). No Hereti page was opened (page budget), so 'kingdom-of-hereti' needs a dossier (Hereti: the Georgian-Albanian marchlands, Arishiani princes). (2) The Principality page dates the union 1010 and the Kingdom page c. 1014; 1014 is used. (3) Abkhazian overlordship of Kakheti: the Abkhazia dossier has it 935-960; this page's 959 Ujarma episode and 'truce with Leon III' are undated. (4) Late 9th century: Hereti's Grigor Hamam conquered parts of Kakheti (no year). (5) Eklez River is 1027 per the Kingdom page. Gazetteer: 'Hereti' and 'Kukheti' are not region names; Hereti is drawn as Azerbaijani admin-1 units (Zaqatala, Balakan, Qax, Sheki), Gardabani as a 25 km circle. wikidata id null (Wikidata unreachable).
